facts.fact: Tom Allen shot Timothy Confoy in his saloon on Market Street in the early hours of Sunday 26 February 1899; Confoy died that night at City Hospital, and John Spencer was wounded in the hand.
facts.conflict: date: 26 February (most claims) vs 20 February (189.c1, 192.c1) and 23 February (180.c1, 180.c4, 180.c6). location: near Sixth and Market (179.c1) or 619 Market Street (985.c1) vs the corner of Seventh and Market (189.c1, 192.c1). victim: named Tom Coupry in 181.c2, 181.c3, 182.c2, 182.c3 and 185.c3 (185.c3 says Coupry was later named in the report as the man shot) vs Timothy Confoy in the rest. Disturbance: 179.c2 says there was no unusual disturbance before Allen drew, vs Allen's account of a movement by Confoy (180.c4, 985.c4, 181.c4, 182.c4). Confoy's pistol: found under him (987.c7, 987.c8, 180.c6) vs dropped on his own revolver (183.c5).

facts.fact: After the shooting Tom Allen was taken into custody, held at the Four Courts holdover, and a coroner's jury on 28 February 1899 returned a verdict of justifiable homicide; he was then charged with second-degree murder and released on bond.
A grand jury indicted Tom Allen for the murder of Tim Confoy on 3 May 1899; he was admitted to bond of $5,000 in Judge Klein's court, with Thomas J. Rowe going bond.
facts.conflict: 186.c4 says Allen was discharged on a plea of self-defense after a preliminary hearing in the Court of Criminal Correction, which sits oddly with the indictment (186.c1) and the bail on 4 May (260.c1, 260.c2); 186.c4 gives only the year 1899

facts.fact: The state dismissed the murder case against Tom Allen for the killing of Timothy Confoy in Judge Fisher's court, the evidence being insufficient.
Police arrested Jesse Carraher, a musician employed in the saloon, on 3 March 1901, pending investigation of a fall.
